notes: Evals assume the subagent runs with cwd set to a real codebase checkout so it can explore architecture while planning. The skill accepts a PRD (default), an approach doc (./docs/approach.md), a roadmap (./roadmap.html), or a raw conversation, and writes a phased tracer-bullet plan to ./plans/. Backward-compat: with a PRD in the conversation it must behave exactly as before. Input detection is delegated to the artifact-scan skill — to-plan references it one level deep rather than re-implementing detection.

evals.name: prd-in-conversation-default
evals.prompt:
Here's the PRD, break it into an implementation plan with tracer bullets.

[PRD] Saved Searches

Problem: Users re-type the same filter queries every visit. We want to let them save a query and re-run it.

User stories:
1. As a user I can save my current search filters under a name.
2. As a user I can see a list of my saved searches and run one with a click.
3. As a user I can delete a saved search.

Out of scope: sharing saved searches between users.
evals.expected_output: A phased tracer-bullet plan written to ./plans/<feature>.md. The PRD path is unchanged: the skill uses the pasted PRD directly, includes a Technical design decisions header (routes, schema, key models, module boundaries, API/interface contracts, integration points), and breaks the work into vertical slices each with User stories and Acceptance criteria. The plan is concrete enough to hand to to-tickets.

assertions.text: A plan file is created under ./plans/ as a Markdown file named after the feature
The skill uses the pasted PRD directly and does NOT ask the user to locate or paste a source (backward-compat: PRD path unchanged)
The plan contains a 'Technical design decisions' section with concrete durable decisions (at least schema shape and module boundaries)
The plan is broken into at least 2 phases, each a vertical slice with a Title, User stories, and Acceptance criteria
Each phase is a thin end-to-end vertical slice cutting through multiple layers, not a horizontal slice of a single layer
The plan is concrete enough for to-tickets to derive tickets without re-deriving the design (contracts/model names/routes are named, not deferred)

evals.name: approach-doc-only-skip-to-plan
evals.prompt: No PRD, but we already aligned on the approach. Skip straight to an implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: With no PRD in the conversation, the skill locates the approach doc at ./docs/approach.md (using artifact-scan as a preflight to find inputs rather than re-implementing detection), and builds the phased tracer-bullet plan from it. Output is the same technical-design plan in ./plans/ with a Technical design decisions header and vertical slices, sourced from the approach doc.

files.content:
# Approach: Offline Mode

## What we are building

An offline mode so the notes app keeps working without a network connection and syncs when it reconnects.

## Why

Users on flaky connections lose edits today. Offline-first removes that failure class.

## Decisions

- Local-first store is the source of truth; the server is a sync target.
- Last-write-wins conflict resolution for the first version; no CRDTs yet.
- Sync runs opportunistically in the background when connectivity returns.

## Features

- Read and edit notes while offline.
- Queue local changes and replay them on reconnect.
- Show a sync status indicator.

## Out of scope

- Real-time collaborative editing.

assertions.text: The skill does NOT stop and demand a PRD; it proceeds to locate an alternative input
The skill locates and reads ./docs/approach.md as the source for the plan
Input detection is delegated to the artifact-scan skill (referenced one level deep), not re-implemented inline in to-plan
A plan file is created under ./plans/ as a Markdown file named after the feature (e.g. offline-mode)
The plan contains a 'Technical design decisions' section and reflects decisions from the approach doc (e.g. local-first store, last-write-wins, background sync)
The plan is broken into vertical-slice phases, each with User stories/features and Acceptance criteria
The plan's Source line references the approach doc rather than a PRD

evals.name: conversation-only-skip-to-plan
evals.prompt:
We just hashed this out in chat, no PRD and no docs yet. Turn it straight into a plan:

Me: I want an export feature so people can download their data as CSV or JSON.
AI: Which entities? All of them or a subset?
Me: Start with the two big ones — projects and tasks. One file per entity type.
AI: Sync download or emailed link?
Me: Sync is fine for now, it's small. Zip the files together.
Me: And gate it behind a feature flag so we can roll it out gradually.
evals.expected_output: With no PRD, approach doc, or roadmap present, the skill uses the pasted conversation as the WHAT/WHY input and builds the phased tracer-bullet plan from it. Output is the same technical-design plan in ./plans/ with a Technical design decisions header and vertical slices derived from the agreed conversation (CSV/JSON export of projects and tasks, zipped sync download, behind a feature flag).

assertions.text: The skill does NOT stop and demand a PRD; it uses the pasted conversation as the source
A plan file is created under ./plans/ as a Markdown file named after the feature (e.g. data-export)
The plan contains a 'Technical design decisions' section with concrete durable decisions
The plan captures the agreed conversation details: CSV and JSON export, projects and tasks entities, zipped synchronous download, feature-flag gating
The plan is broken into vertical-slice phases, each with User stories/features and Acceptance criteria
The plan is concrete enough for to-tickets to derive tickets without re-deriving the design
